facet_selection_reasoning: This combination focuses on the conceptual foundations of the sampling distribution that determine the validity and characteristics of a confidence interval. It specifically targets the relationship between standard error and interval width (A7) while diagnosticating misconceptions about whether the sampling distribution is identical to the sample (B8), whether it always mirrors the population shape (B9), or whether it is always normal regardless of sample size (B12).

item.stem: The distribution of weekly grocery expenses in a city is known to be highly skewed with a population standard deviation (σ) of $40. A researcher plans to take a sample of 16 households to calculate a 95% confidence interval for the mean expense. Which of the following is true?

options.text: The current standard error is $10; if the researcher increased the sample size to 100, the standard error would decrease to $4, which would result in a narrower confidence interval.
options.rationale: The student correctly calculates the standard error (40 / sqrt(16) = 10) and understands that increasing the sample size reduces the standard error (40 / sqrt(100) = 4), which in turn decreases the width of the confidence interval.

options.text: The sampling distribution for this study is simply the distribution of the 16 individual grocery expenses collected in the sample.
options.rationale: The student confuses the sampling distribution (the distribution of all possible sample means) with the sample distribution (the distribution of data points within a single sample).

options.text: The standard error for this study is $40, because the sampling distribution of the mean mirrors the standard deviation found in the underlying population.
options.rationale: The student incorrectly believes the standard deviation of the sampling distribution (standard error) is equal to the population standard deviation, ignoring the impact of the sample size (n).

options.text: The sampling distribution of the mean is guaranteed to be Normal in this case because the distribution of sample means always follows a normal distribution regardless of the population shape or sample size.
options.rationale: The student incorrectly assumes that the sampling distribution is always Normally distributed, failing to recognize that for a skewed population, a larger sample size (typically n > 30) is needed for the sampling distribution to approach normality.

item.explanation: This item assesses the understanding of the standard error's relationship to confidence interval width and common misconceptions about the nature of the sampling distribution. The correct answer (A) recognizes that standard error is σ/√n and that a smaller standard error leads to a more precise (narrower) interval (A7). Distractor B addresses the confusion between sample and sampling distributions (B8). Distractor C addresses the belief that the sampling distribution has the same spread as the population (B9). Distractor D addresses the misconception that the sampling distribution is always Normal regardless of sample size or population shape (B12).
